name: Consumed by Greed
description:
Each opponent draws a card.

Sacrifice target creature with the greatest power. Return X target creature cards from your graveyard to your hand.
assumptions: Treated the card's three flow roots (A, C, D) as producing at most two printed paragraphs, in the order they appear in `roots` (C, then D): node A (the cast itself, `to: "stack"`) is followed only by B, a bare `move` of the card from stack to graveyard — ordinary post-resolution housekeeping every instant does, not printed text — so A/B contributes no paragraph of its own.

Folded D and E into a single paragraph: D's own `to` is "gy", not "stack", so the D→E step is a guaranteed, non-interruptible continuation rather than a second stack object. I read the schema's "trigger/arrival condition vs. printed-effect-after-a-stack-node" split as written primarily for triggered abilities; applied to this trigger-less two-step spell chain, I took the whole non-stack chain as one uninterrupted printed effect rather than trying to force it into an arrival/effect split that doesn't apply here.
Assumed sibling roots (C, D) print in the order listed in `roots`, since the schema defines dependency, not left-to-right print order, between independent roots.
couldNotDerive: What determines the value of X in node E's `qty:X..X`. No node carries a `:=` binding that names or fixes this count (e.g., nothing ties it explicitly to the power of the creature sacrificed in D), so the graph confirms only that E returns a single fixed-but-variable number of creature cards, not what that number equals.

Whether `cond:greatest_power` on D means strictly the single greatest-power creature or also covers ties for greatest — the flag doesn't distinguish, so I used the plain "with the greatest power" wording without resolving the tie case.
notes: Second attempt, after real translator fixes were applied to edges.json between rounds. Mana cost {1}{B}{B} and type Instant match the self registry and the real card (forge-model/data/consumed-by-greed.txt) exactly, and the two-paragraph shape/order (draw effect, then sacrifice+return effect) now lines up with the real Oracle text's own two lines. Concrete improvement over attempt 1: node D was previously owner:"me" with only flags:"cond:sacrifice" (misread as the caster sacrificing an unconstrained creature of their own); it is now owner:"any" with flags:"target cond:greatest_power cond:sacrifice", and the reconstructing agent correctly produced "Sacrifice target creature with the greatest power" this round — the missing greatest-power selection criterion (Forge's `SacValid$ Creature.greatestPowerControlledByTargeted`) and the targeting fact are both now present in the decomposition and both surfaced correctly in the blind reconstruction. Two issues remain open, both pre-flagged as known/deliberately-unfixed rather than new findings: (1) Gift's optionality and single-opponent framing — node C is still `owner:"opp"` with no flags at all (no `may`, no `target`), which per the registry's own stated meaning of owner:opp ("every opponent, symmetric") reads as an unconditional "each opponent draws a card" rather than Forge's actual `K:Gift`/`GiftAbility` (caster may promise the gift to one target opponent as part of casting; if promised, that opponent draws before the spell's other effects). The agent's "Each opponent draws a card" is the correct, faithful reading of node C exactly as currently encoded — this is a decomposition/schema gap, not a reconstruction error. (2) The dynamic return-count binding — node E's `qty:X..X` still has no `:=`/`=` binding anywhere in the flow tying X to whether the gift was promised (real card: `SVar:X:Count$PromisedGift.1.0`, i.e. X=1 if promised else X=0); the D→E step structurally implies the return follows the sacrifice, but nothing implies it depends on C's occurrence at all. The agent again correctly declined to invent a value for X and listed it under "Could not derive" rather than guessing — same expected behavior as attempt 1. Minor residual wording note, not a new mechanic gap: the reconstruction says "Sacrifice target creature with the greatest power" (creature itself sounds directly targeted) rather than the real card's "Target opponent sacrifices a creature with the greatest power among creatures they control" (opponent is the target; the creature is selected by criterion, not targeted) — this ambiguity falls directly out of node D packing both "who is targeted" and "what moves" onto one owner:any+target node, and is a byproduct of the same known single-target-opponent nuance already called out above, not a separate defect.
